chestnut_gpu.title: The Chestnut GPU Series (Big Models)
chestnut_gpu.subtitle: eGPU-Only Heavyweights
chestnut_gpu.includes: Cinque Terre, BMRLNAP v6/v4/v3/v2/v1, Sad Model, Happy Birthday, I Desire, Tee Time, TTTTFBRLM, Lebowski
chestnut_gpu.vibe: These are the "big models" — chestnut-class networks larger than anything in the WMI or OP lines, tied to comma's new GPU add-on, which began reaching owners in August 2026. They drop under the forum's big_model tag on a near-daily cadence during a run. The extra network size shows up first in lateral: taking in-town 90-degree turns wide instead of cutting them, and showing planted rather than floaty highway stability. Standout entries like Cinque Terre and Sad Model have significantly improved lateral stability and natural steering feel, while earlier BMRLNAP runs suffered from low-speed steering oscillations. Stop signs and traffic light stop lines remain an active area of tuning across the line.
chestnut_gpu.bestFor: Chestnut owners with an eGPU who want the largest available networks and are comfortable testing.
chestnut_gpu.recommendation: Cinque Terre Model (CTM) is the top-rated big model for solid lateral stability and daily experimental driving. BMRLNAP v4 remains a proven community workhorse for highway cut-in response, while Sad Model is great for natural steering. Avoid BMRLNAP v3 due to severe low-speed steering oscillations.

wmi_2026.title: The WMI & 2026 World Series (The Modern Standard)
wmi_2026.subtitle: End-to-End Intelligence
wmi_2026.includes: WMI V12, V11, V10, SC Model, Macrostiff
wmi_2026.vibe: These are the cutting edge. 'WMI' likely stands for 'World Model Iteration.' These models use the latest End-to-End (E2E) architecture, meaning they 'see' the world more like a human. They understand 3D scenes, stop signs, intersections, and road edges - not just painted lines. WMI V12 is the current flagship. It's the smartest at complex urban scenarios but can feel slightly 'loose' on straight highways because it's constantly micro-adjusting like a human driver would. If you drive mostly city streets with stop signs and turns, this is your series.
wmi_2026.bestFor: Daily driving in 2026. They balance smoothness with intelligence.
wmi_2026.recommendation: Start with WMI V12. If it feels too 'wiggly' on highways, try Macrostiff for tighter steering feel.

aggressive.title: The Aggressive Series
aggressive.subtitle: Traffic Warriors
aggressive.includes: Dark Souls Model, Dark Souls v2, Firehose
aggressive.vibe: High-performance, high-attention. Dark Souls is named because it's 'unforgiving' or 'hardcore.' Expect tighter following distances, faster acceleration, and sharper turns. It drives like a human who is in a hurry but still safe. Great for heavy trucks (F-150s, Sierras) that need authoritative inputs to move their mass. The Firehose model is the raw, unfiltered developer feed from comma.ai's State-of-the-Art (SOTA) training runs. It represents the absolute 'bleeding edge' of model development, updating almost daily as new data is ingested from the global fleet.
aggressive.bestFor: Heavy traffic commuters (Dark Souls) or adventurous testers (Firehose).
aggressive.recommendation: Dark Souls v2 for trucks and SUVs. Only try Firehose if you want to test the newest, potentially unstable SOTA iterations before they are finalized.

comfort.title: The Comfort & Smooth Series
comfort.subtitle: Passenger Friendly
comfort.includes: Down to Ride (DTR), Space Lab, Kumars Vibe
comfort.vibe: Relaxed and passenger-friendly. Down to Ride (DTR) is famous for being 'wife-approved.' It prioritizes gentle braking and slow turns over perfect lane centering. Kumars Vibe is custom-tuned for a specific car setup but became popular because it removes the 'robotic' feel - very natural steering transitions. These models are perfect for road trips where passengers might get motion sick from abrupt steering corrections.
comfort.bestFor: Road trips with family or passengers who get motion sick.
comfort.recommendation: Start with Down to Ride v6. It's the community's go-to for passenger comfort.

tomb_raider.title: The Tomb Raider / Trash Folder (TR) Series
tomb_raider.subtitle: Hidden Gems
tomb_raider.vibe: These are experimental training runs. Despite the name, some are hidden gems! Tomb Raider 16 (Trash Folder 16) was a community favorite for a long time due to its unique handling of highway curves. It felt like driving 'on rails.' These models often have quirks but can surprise you with excellent performance in specific scenarios. Worth trying if you drive curvy roads.
tomb_raider.bestFor: Adventurous users looking for unique driving characteristics.
tomb_raider.recommendation: Tomb Raider 16 for winding backroads. Don't let the 'Trash Folder' name scare you!

legacy.title: The Legacy Legends
legacy.subtitle: Old Reliable
legacy.includes: Recertified Herbalist, North Dakota, Blue Diamond
legacy.vibe: The 'Old Guard.' These models are from 2023-2024. They are less 'smart' (bad at stop signs) but incredible at highway lane keeping. Recertified Herbalist is the 'Gold Standard' of stability. North Dakota is famous for its STIFF steering - it hugs the center of the lane and refuses to move. WD40 'lubricated' this stiffness for smoother inputs. Blue Diamond excels in rain and poor lane markings. These are the 'Toyota Camry' of models - boring, reliable, and rock solid.
legacy.bestFor: Highway-focused driving with rock-solid lane centering.
legacy.recommendation: Recertified Herbalist for long road trips. North Dakota if you want maximum stiffness.

opm.title: The OPM Series (Off-Policy Models)
opm.subtitle: Learning from Corrections
opm.includes: OP Model 10 v3 (latest), OP Model 10 v2/v1, OP Model 7-9, Off-Policy Model v1-v5
opm.vibe: These models use off-policy training — they learn from moments where the model's behavior differed from the human driver's corrections, rather than just cloning driving behavior. This allows them to learn more effectively from edge cases. They show improved highway centering and quicker lateral recentering compared to standard WMI models, though longitudinal control is still being refined.
opm.bestFor: Highway-focused driving with improved lane centering.
opm.recommendation: OP Model 10 v3 is the current pick of the latest 10-series — v1 was rough, v2 fixed braking but stalled off the line, and v3 brought DEC-level acceleration back. Be aware that low-speed performance and turns may still vary by vehicle.

categories.name: Favorites
categories.description: The most popular models for daily driving right now. Community-tested and approved.

models.name: TCPmV3 (The Cool Peoples Model)
models.consensus: Highly praised community model known for its exceptional smoothness and lack of low-speed jerkiness. Many users describe it as 'awesome' and superior to standard releases for lateral control consistency.
models.note: Particularly popular with Kia e-Niro users in the UK. One of the best custom lateral models of late 2025.
positives: No low-speed jerkiness
Excellent lateral control
Ultra-smooth transitions
Stabilizes speed in E2E
Works well with NNLC
negatives: Late braking (experimental long)
Hugs turns tight
Hugs left at night without lead car

models.name: WMI V12
models.consensus: The current flagship and daily driver for most users in 2026. Highest intelligence for complex scenarios like intersections, stop signs, and tight urban turns.
models.note: Can feel slightly 'loose' on straight highways.

models.name: Dark Souls Model v2
models.consensus: The 'unforgiving' model, refined. Tighter following distance, faster reactions, sharper turns. Excellent for larger vehicles that need authority.
models.note: Named 'Dark Souls' because it's unforgiving.

models.name: Nevada Model
models.consensus: The 'neutral' benchmark. If a new model feels weird, Nevada is what you compare it to. Well-balanced between smooth and responsive.

models.name: Down to Ride v6
models.consensus: The legendary 'Wife Approved' model. Sacrifices perfect lane centering for passenger comfort. Won't jerk the wheel; gently drifts into turns. Note: Some Comma 4 users (specifically Ioniq 5) report pronounced right-side lane hugging.
models.note: Perfect for road trips. If hugging right on C4, try Adjust Camera Offset (-0.05 to -0.10).

categories.name: Chestnut GPU
categories.description: Chestnut-class "big" driving models — larger networks tied to comma's new GPU add-on, which began shipping to owners in August 2026. Released under the forum's big_model tag on a near-daily cadence during a run.

models.name: Cinque Terre Model
models.consensus: Early community standout hailed on Discord and Discourse as the most usable and stable big model to date ('Best model I've ever used by a mile', 'Would make POP v2 proud'). Testers report that lateral control feels solid and 'on rails' across all speeds (0-65 mph), closely rivaling Firehose, with low-speed oscillation drastically dampened compared to the violent wobbles of the BMRLNAP series. Successfully obeys stop signs and red lights in experimental mode, though some testers note eager acceleration and occasional highway speed deficits without dynamic experimental control.
models.note: Chestnut-class big model (CTM), built from 68b5f8e in commaai/openpilot. Part of the 2026 Deep RL Models. Requires comma four or comma 3X with comma chestnut eGPU. 100% of survey respondents voted 'Better' than default BMRLNAP v4 and recommended merging as default. High network transfer overhead (~700MB model size) prompted sunnypilot developer optimization (PR #1993 / PR #1998) to prevent DMA frame drops.
models.bestFor: Experimental Mode / Daily Driving / Lateral Stability
positives: Planted lateral steering and centering authority comparable to Firehose across all speeds
Substantially cures the severe low-speed steering oscillations seen in BMRLNAP v3/v4/v6
Reliable stop light and stop sign obedience in experimental mode
Quick, authoritative acceleration off the line praised by aggressive longitudinal drivers
negatives: Requires updated dev-chestnut build (PR #1993) to avoid initial model lagging / frame drop warnings during DMA CPU-to-GPU transfer
Can run a few mph under set speed on highways in pure experimental mode without dynamic experimental control
Minor low-speed oscillation still slightly perceptible under 12 mph (though greatly reduced)
Large ~700MB download size can take several minutes on slower comma Wi-Fi links

models.name: BMRLNAP Model v6
models.consensus: Direct successor to BMRLNAP Model v4 (v5 was skipped). Early community feedback reports that longitudinal deceleration and stopping behavior at traffic lights have improved slightly compared to v4, though vehicles can still creep slightly over the line. Lateral stability retains the planted highway cruising feel of v4.
models.note: Chestnut-class big model, built from 9d683c0 in commaai/openpilot. Built in-house by sunnypilot. Compares directly against BMRLNAP v4 to evaluate stop-line precision and deceleration tuning.
positives: Improved traffic light deceleration and stopping behavior over v4
Retains smooth and planted high-speed highway cruising
Active developer responsiveness and in-house tuning
negatives: Still tends to creep slightly across the stop line at traffic lights
Lateral control requires fine-tuning on select Honda builds

models.name: BMRLNAP Model v4
models.consensus: Major evolution in the BMRLNAP series that completely cures the severe low-speed steering oscillations of v3. Outstanding in highway cruising, lead-car following, and handling sudden cut-ins with calm, gradual deceleration rather than harsh brake stabbing. Testers note that curve handling performs better when disabling legacy SCC-V curvature deceleration, though sharp intersection 90-degree turns can still understeer due to steering torque limits, and acceleration from a standstill at green lights remains slow.
models.note: Chestnut-class big model, built from f877d7a in commaai/openpilot. High engagement across Discord and Discourse. Community reports highlight significant vehicle controller sensitivity on Toyotas (Torque v0 vs v1).
positives: Completely resolves the low-speed see-saw steering oscillations from v3
Exceptional, calm, confidence-inspiring handling of sudden highway cut-ins
Smooth longitudinal deceleration without abrupt brake stabbing
Capable of maneuvering around illegally parked obstacles in E2E mode
negatives: Understeers or gives up halfway through sharp 90-degree intersection turns
Sluggish acceleration off the line when a red light turns green
Severe controller sensitivity reported on Toyota with Torque controller v1

models.name: Sad Model
models.consensus: Dedicated farewell drop for comma researcher Toby that earned zero negative ratings from community testers (80% Good or Great). Praised for unanimously smooth acceleration and deceleration with no jerky surging or stop line overshoots. Steering feels natural, humanlike, and stable with no ping-pong, though drivers note a slight tendency to cut corners tight on certain curves.
models.note: Chestnut-class big model, built from 30de303 in commaai/openpilot. Released to commemorate comma research engineer Toby's final driving model contribution.
models.bestFor: Natural Steering Feel / Gentle Long Cruising
positives: Unanimously smooth acceleration and braking across all poll voters
Natural, humanlike steering without wander or low-speed oscillation
Zero Bad or Poor ratings from community testers
Smooth and reliable stop sign and light deceleration
negatives: Tends to cut corners slightly tight on inside curves
Minor lane hugging to one side noted by select drivers

models.name: BMRLNAP Model v3
models.consensus: Severely plagued by low-speed steering oscillations and see-sawing that testers humorously compared to actors fake-steering in old movies. While open-highway cruising and longitudinal braking are smooth, the low-speed wheel oscillation was pronounced across Prius, Civic, Accord, and Rivian test vehicles, prompting testers to recommend skipping forward to v4.
models.note: Chestnut-class big model, built from 47377ac in commaai/openpilot. High-speed highway cruising is acceptable, but low-speed oscillation makes it unsuitable as a daily driver.
positives: Smooth longitudinal acceleration and braking once up to cruising speeds
Stable lead-car following on open multi-lane highway
negatives: Aggressive low-speed steering wheel oscillations ('see-sawing')
Understeers and gives up in the second half of sharp intersection turns
Tends to roll stop signs as California stops

models.name: BMRLNAP Model v2
models.consensus: Second iteration of the BMRLNAP big model line. Highway lanekeeping, cut-in reaction, and high-speed cloverleaf centering are solid and natural across Kia EV6, Elantra, and Camry testers. However, city driving shows mixed results, with testers reporting inconsistent stopping distances at traffic lights and a tendency to stop too close behind lead cars.
models.note: Chestnut-class big model, tied to comma's new GPU add-on. Tested across Kia EV6, 2022 Hyundai Elantra, and 2023 Camry XSE.
positives: Smooth, natural lateral control and responsive cut-in avoidance on highway
Cloverleaf on/off ramps handled smoothly without inside-line hugging
Quick acceleration response off the line
negatives: Inconsistent stopping at traffic light white lines and signs above 55 mph
Stops too close for comfort behind lead cars at red lights
Noticeable regression in city stop consistency compared to v1

models.name: Happy Birthday Model
models.consensus: Special release drop commemorating sunnyhaibin's birthday. Discord testers praised its gentle stop-and-go behavior in heavy traffic and natural cruising feel, though high-speed braking into sudden red lights remains somewhat late.
models.note: Dedicated to sunnypilot founder sunnyhaibin on his birthday (August 24). Community testers report pleasant stop-and-go cruising on Chestnut hardware.
positives: Smooth, natural feel in stop-and-go traffic
Strong low-speed lead car following and light detection
Pleasant, non-robotic steering feel
negatives: Brakes somewhat late and fast into sudden reds at high speeds

models.name: I Desire Model
models.consensus: Strongest early reception of the big model run: 75% Good or better on a small four-vote poll, and the only unanimous longitudinal result so far — both voters picked 'smooth acceleration & braking', with no votes for jerky, hard/late or bad stop-and-go. Praised for planted, non-floaty lanekeeping and cruising with none of the long oscillations that cause motion sickness. Traffic lights and stop signs are the consistent weak point, and the lateral poll splits evenly between 'smooth & steady' and lane hugging / ping-pong.
models.note: Chestnut-class model, tied to comma's new GPU add-on. Vote counts are still tiny (4 on the headline poll, 2-3 on the detail polls), so treat the score as provisional. One reporter ran it on a dash-mounted C4 and a C3X; another tested a 2023 Camry on rural roads.
positives: Great lanekeeping and cruising; planted rather than floaty
Unanimous smooth acceleration & braking in the longitudinal poll
No long oscillations that cause motion sickness
Still sees stop signs in time and slows appropriately
negatives: Traffic lights and stop signs are its achilles heel
Rolling stops — a full stop at only 1 of 10 signs on one drive
Hesitant acceleration at speed, settling at 53 mph on 55 mph roads
Slows for cross roads that have no stop or yield sign
Typical slow-speed oscillation, with wandering ping-pong on some roads

models.name: BMRLNAP Model
models.consensus: Best received drop of the big model run, but on only two voters: a unanimous 5-Great headline poll, unanimous 'smooth & steady' lateral and unanimous smooth acceleration & braking. A sunnypilot developer called it 'literally definition of end to end'. Longitudinal is the standout — holds speed well at 60, gets back on the gas quickly when a red turns green, and responds well to yellows it cannot clear. Stop signs are the caveat: it arrives slightly too fast to stop at or before the sign, and a dusk drive rolled noticeably more of them and needed intervention.
models.note: Chestnut-class model, tied to comma's new GPU add-on. The score comes from a unanimous but two-vote poll, so it is provisional and not comparable with the larger-sample entries — the detail polls have the same two voters. The fullest report is a 2023 Camry, whose driver planned to daily-drive it despite the dusk-drive stop-sign rolling.
positives: Unanimous 5-Great headline poll and unanimous smooth & steady lateral
Unanimous smooth acceleration & braking in the longitudinal poll
Holds speed well even at 60 mph
Very fast back on the gas when a red light turns green
Very good response to yellow lights it cannot clear
negatives: Approaches stop signs from 60 mph slightly too fast to stop at or before the sign
Rolled noticeably more stop signs on a dusk drive and needed intervention
Stopping position at night sits a little too far forward at signs and lights
Late reaction to traffic cones directing traffic into a new lane
A little wandering, with small left hugging on narrower roads

models.name: Tee Time Model
models.consensus: The most divided drop of the run: a four-vote poll split evenly between Good and Bad, and the only entry whose lateral poll returned no positive votes at all — ping-pong/wanders at two of three voters, lane hugging and over-steering in curves at one each, nothing for smooth & steady or natural. Ping-pong is called very noticeable at high speed. Longitudinal reads contradictory until you separate smoothness from judgement: the poll is unanimous for smooth acceleration and braking, while the written feedback is all about slowing far too early — bleeding a 55 mph road down to about 48 and dipping at every crossroads or cluster of houses. The standout is low-speed stop signs, described as the best seen on any model below 50 mph, stopping smoothly just before the sign 9 or 10 times back to back; above that speed a tester disengages because it no longer sees them in time.
models.note: Chestnut-class model, tied to comma's new GPU add-on. Headline poll is four voters, evenly split Good and Bad. Read the polls and the comments together: the longitudinal poll is unanimously positive while the prose complains about over-early slowing, so that poll option is measuring smoothness rather than whether the timing is appropriate. Fullest report is a 2023 Camry.
positives: Stop sign performance below 50 mph called the best seen on any model
Stops smoothly just before the sign, 9 or 10 times back to back
Unanimous smooth acceleration & braking in the longitudinal poll
Moves away from centre when oncoming traffic approaches
negatives: No positive lateral votes at all — ping-pong/wanders at two of three voters
Ping-pong very noticeable at high speed
Slows so early it becomes uncomfortable in city driving
Bleeds speed on a 55 mph road and settles around 48
Above 50 mph it cannot see stop signs in time, prompting disengagement

models.name: TTTTFBRLM
models.consensus: First of the mid-August big model run. Notable for a reported 'Big Model Error' that forces an immediate takeover roughly one minute after engagement on some Chestnut setups.
models.note: Chestnut-class model, tied to comma's new GPU add-on. Hardware began reaching owners in August 2026. A separate Driving Issues thread tracks a 'Big Model Error' takeover prompt on sunnypilot 2026.003.000.
negatives: Reported 'Big Model Error' takeover about one minute into engagement

models.name: Lebowski Model
models.consensus: The run's opening drop and a clean split between axes: lateral is the strength, longitudinal is not. A sunnypilot developer calls the lateral 'outstanding' and far more confident on right and left turns than the small models, and a tester on a 2022 Rivian R1T reports in-town 90-degree-plus turns taken appropriately wide, much less prone to cutting corners and curbing the wheels. Longitudinal is where it falls apart: hard or late braking tops the longitudinal poll, and once at set speed testers report a gas-brake surging effect. Stop signs are recognised better than on the small models but still missed occasionally, and rolled as California stops when seen.
models.note: Described by a tester as the first iteration of a chestnut-class model. Headline poll is four voters. This thread also pins the hardware timeline: a reader asked how people were running it without the new GPU add-on, and the founder replied that comma chestnut units were being delivered that week, with another tester saying he had had his since the week before. Tested on a 2022 Rivian R1T with the angle-steering harness.
positives: Outstanding lateral — confident on right and left turns, unlike the small models
Takes in-town 90-degree-plus turns appropriately wide, far less likely to curb the wheels
Accelerates from a stop better than the smaller models
Begins decelerating much sooner, stopping comfortably and naturally
Recognises stop signs better than the small models
negatives: Hard or late braking tops the longitudinal poll, at two of three voters
Gas-brake surging once it settles at set speed
Still misses some stop signs, and does a California stop at those it sees
Lane hugging reported by every lateral voter

categories.name: WMI 2026
categories.description: Latest End-to-End architecture. Understands 3D scenes, stop signs, and complex intersections.

models.name: OP Model 10 v3
models.consensus: Strong rebound for the OP Model 10 line. Acceleration is reported as on par with DEC ('accelerates just as well') — a clear fix for v1/v2's sluggish off-the-line behavior. Early daily-driver impressions describe it as 'great' and the recommended pick across v1/v2/v3.
models.note: Referenced in the OP Model 9 thread as the supersession that received significantly better feedback. Recommended over v1 and v2.
positives: DEC-level acceleration in Experimental Mode
Resolves v2's sluggish stops
Reviewer plans to daily-drive it

models.name: OP Model 10 v2
models.consensus: Major step up from v1. Longitudinal feel is the highlight — the softest, most consistent braking the reviewer has felt in a while. Lateral still hugs left (fixable with camera offset) and the model remains slow to straighten the wheel after sharp turns.
models.note: Hugs-left can be mitigated with camera offset +0.05 to +0.10. Some lingering hesitation off the line and slow wheel return after corners.
positives: Softest, most consistent braking in a while
Solid longitudinal control
Reaches cruise speed well
negatives: Hesitant to accelerate from a stop
Left-lane hugging
Slow to straighten wheel after sharp turns

models.name: OP Model v10
models.consensus: Initial release of the OP Model 10 line received strongly negative early feedback. Reviewers cite poor lateral control with late corrections that snap dramatically after the car has already left the lane line. No positives reported.
models.note: Quickly superseded by v2 and v3. Skip directly to v3 for the recommended option.
negatives: Late lane corrections
Dramatic hard snaps after leaving lane lines
Frequently drives outside the painted lane

models.name: OP Model 9
models.consensus: Community feedback is overwhelmingly negative with 9 voters. 44% rated 'Bad', 44% rated 'Horrible', and only 11% rated 'Ok'. Users report the model should be 'removed/reverted' as it is 'quite bad'. No positive reviews have been submitted.
models.note: Not recommended for daily driving. Superseded by OP Model 10 v3 which received significantly better feedback.
negatives: Unstable lateral control
Unanimously negative feedback
Does not resolve previous OP model issues

models.name: OP Model 8
models.consensus: Early community feedback is predominantly negative. Users report twitchy, oscillating steering at high speeds, difficulty maintaining lane in stop-and-go traffic, and consistent left-lane hugging. The model appears to struggle with the lateral stability that OP Model 7 had improved.
models.note: Left-hugging is a consistent issue. If trying this model, adjust camera offset (+0.05 to +0.10). Not recommended for daily driving at this stage.
negatives: Twitchy / oscillating steering at high speeds
Struggles to maintain lane in stop-and-go traffic
Consistent left-lane hugging

models.name: OP Model 7
models.consensus: Significant leap forward for the Off-Policy series. Praised as the most confident OP model yet, with smoother longitudinal deceleration for stopped leads and improved lateral control that self-corrects even when overshooting sharp 90-degree turns. However, random left-hugging persists for some users.
models.note: Best lateral of the series so far. If hugging left, adjust camera offset (+0.05).
positives: Excellent lateral self-correction
Smooth stops for leads
Quick acceleration
negatives: Random left-hugging for some
Inconsistent city speed
Jerky steering on specific angle cars

models.name: OP Model
models.consensus: Very early model drop with limited community feedback so far. Initial votes lean positive (Good) but sample size is extremely small. Needs more testing and community evaluation before drawing conclusions.
models.note: Very few votes so far — check back for updated consensus as more users test it.

models.name: Pop v2
models.consensus: Highly polarizing release with growing negative sentiment. Longitudinal control is praised by some (smooth stops behind leads on GV60), but multiple reports of 'afraid of green lights' behavior and failure to stay stopped at red lights. Lateral unwind is improved but stiffer steering causes oscillations and motion sickness on some vehicles. Very vehicle-dependent — F-150 Lightning reports twitchy low-speed behavior.
models.note: Vehicle dependent. Great on GV60, twitchy on F-150 Lightning. Subaru Crosstrek users report motion sickness. Torque Tune v0 recommended.
positives: Better lateral unwind
Smooth stops behind leads (GV60)
Improved longitudinal for some
negatives: Afraid of green lights
Fails to stay stopped at red lights
Twitchy at low speeds (F-150 Lightning)
Stiffer steering causes oscillations
Yoyo following distance
Motion sickness inducing on some vehicles

models.name: Pop Model
models.consensus: Community sentiment has warmed significantly with more testing. Lateral control is vehicle-dependent — Honda Civic users report the best lat in a while with no ping-pong and centering 'like it owes the lane lines money,' while Hyundai Kona and others experience extreme line-to-line ping-ponging above 50mph. More willing to reach set speeds than Pop v2. Still known for creeping at red lights.
models.note: Very vehicle-dependent. Honda/Kia users trending positive. Torque tune version matters — test with v0 first.
positives: Confident lateral on some vehicles
Quick recentering
Good 90-degree turn handling
Stays stopped at red lights
11/10 lateral on Kia Niro
More willing to reach set speeds
negatives: Extreme ping-pong on some vehicles above 50mph
Speeds aggressively without a lead car
Jerky/octagonal curve handling
Creeps at red lights

models.name: CD210 Model
models.consensus: Based on WMI V12 architecture with subtle differences. Shows improved red light stopping behavior and less ping-pong at low speeds. However, multiple users report pronounced oversteering on turns — especially problematic on Toyota vehicles with low-torque EPS. Hard braking at close range and red light creeping are also noted drawbacks.
models.note: Vehicle-dependent: praised on Hyundai Ioniq 5, but struggles with Toyota RAV4 Prime. Consider enabling 'pause lateral while turning' if oversteering is an issue.

models.name: WMI V11
models.consensus: Slightly more stable than V12 on straightaways. Good fallback if V12 feels too jittery.
models.note: Preferred for mostly-highway commutes.

models.name: WMI v10
models.consensus: Well-tested mid-generation model. A solid choice if V11/V12 have issues on your specific vehicle.

models.name: SC Model
models.consensus: Likely 'Space Cat' or 'Stable Control' variant. Testing new stability algorithms.
models.note: Worth trying if you want something different.

models.name: WMI V9
models.consensus: Rock-solid choice for newer 2025+ platforms (e.g., Kia K4). Currently the default pre-installed model on Comma 4 hardware. Favored for its stability and predictive behavior on modern ADAS architectures.

models.name: WMI V8
models.consensus: Early 2026 build that established the foundation. Still functional for conservative E2E users.

models.name: WMI V7
models.consensus: New Year's release that kick-started the 2026 WMI series. Historical significance.

models.name: Macrostiff Model
models.consensus: World Model tuned for STIFFER steering response. If WMI V12 feels too 'wiggly', this locks it down.
models.note: Great for vehicles with loose steering racks.

models.name: OP Model 16 Deep
models.consensus: Features an expanded neural network architecture in the OP model lineup. Offers superior spatial perception in messy city driving and multi-lane intersections, though requires modern comma 4 hardware for optimal compute latency.
models.note: Optimized for Comma 4. Recommended for dense suburban and urban environments.
positives: Significantly improved multi-lane awareness and intersection tracking
Handles complex road markings and construction barrels well
Confident steering torque on mid-speed turns
negatives: Higher compute overhead on older comma 3X hardware
Can brake abruptly for pedestrians close to the curb

models.name: Michael RL V2
models.consensus: The next evolution in reinforcement learning driving models following Deep_RL V3. Delivers exceptionally natural steering wheel movement and proactive curve anticipation, mimicking human driving dynamics closely.
models.note: Best suited for openpilot experimental branches and drivers who prefer fluid, human-like dynamics over rigid centering.
positives: Human-like lane positioning with intuitive inside-corner apexing
Progressive and smooth longitudinal braking anticipation
Fluid steering corrections without mechanical micro-adjustments
negatives: Can cut corners slightly closer than rule-based models
Occasional hesitation when lane markings split or end abruptly

models.name: Rebel Legion Model
models.consensus: The highway-focused twin to the Rebel series. Trades aggressive turn torque for rock-steady straight-line tracking and smooth lane changes with minimal wander.
models.note: Recommended for highway commuters looking for a more composed alternative to early WMI models.
positives: Locked-in highway centering with minimal wandering
Smooth lane transitions during openpilot lane changes
Conservative lead vehicle follow distance
negatives: Less aggressive on sharp urban turns than Rebellious Hope
Relatively conservative acceleration from complete stops

models.name: Get Your Hopes Up Model
models.consensus: Early precursor to Rebellious Hope in the Rebel series. Explored high-angle curve tracking with responsive lateral inputs.
models.note: Precursor to Rebellious Hope. Recommended to test Rebellious Hope for latest refinements.
positives: Good curve turn-in
Active steering engagement
negatives: Low-speed wander on some vehicles

models.name: Rebellious Hope Model
models.consensus: Designed to handle aggressive cornering where vehicle torque limits are exceeded without blowing through lane lines like CD210. Delivers strong lane retention through bends, though some vehicles experience low-speed lateral ping-ponging.
models.note: Great for routes with challenging curves. If experiencing low-speed wander, toggle pause lateral on low speeds.
positives: Maintains lane line integrity during high-torque assisted cornering better than CD210
Firm on-center feel when taking aggressive bends
Predictable deceleration profile into turns
negatives: Low-speed lateral ping-pong / oscillations reported on Lexus and some Toyota platforms
Slightly jerky transition when driver intervenes on torque-limited turns

models.name: Terrible Super Fantastic Do Over Model
models.consensus: Split reception on a 12-vote poll: 58% land at Good or better, but a quarter sit at Bad or Horrible. Longitudinal is the strong half — called 'really impressive' in stop-and-go traffic. Lateral is the weak half, drawing reports of hugging the inside of corners, an inability to take intersection turns at all, and sweeping turns that drift wide enough to path off-road.
models.note: Re-cut of the August 12 Terrible Super Fantastic Model. Feedback is polarized rather than lukewarm — the votes cluster at both ends, so expect vehicle-dependent results.
positives: Longitudinal praised as one of the smoothest yet; sees stopped leads and lights far ahead with no harsh brake stabbing
Impressive smooth stop-and-go cruising in heavy traffic
58% community poll rating of Good or Great
negatives: Hugs left on several vehicles, wandering close to the lane line below 6 mph
Sloppy on sharper curves and intersection turns, requiring occasional driver takeover

models.name: Terrible Super Fantastic Model
models.consensus: Mid-August standard-hardware drop, superseded three days later by the 'Do Over' re-cut.

models.name: RDF Model v2
models.consensus: Follow-up to the August 5 RDF Model. Second iteration of the same line on standard hardware.

models.name: RDF Model
models.consensus: Tuned by Yassine/MVL with noticeable longitudinal gains over POP and CD210. Offers smooth stop-and-go speed matching and assertive curve tracking on sweeping highways. Some users report slight low-speed lateral wiggles and reduced torque on high-angle curves for certain steer setups.
models.note: Pair with recent MVL tunings if driving Honda/Hyundai platforms. Very solid longitudinal control in experimental mode.
positives: Substantial acceleration and stopping improvements over POP and CD210
Smooth highway stop & go and speed matching
Assertive steering power and curve handling on long sweeping curves
Strong longitudinal lead detection
negatives: Gives up on sharp high-angle curves on some heavy/angle vehicles (Rivian R1T)
Minor low-speed lateral oscillation/wiggle while vehicle self-tunes
Perpendicular traffic cutting across path can cause abrupt deceleration

categories.name: OPM Models
categories.description: Off-Policy Models learn from driver corrections rather than just cloning behavior, enabling smarter highway centering and recentering.

models.name: Off-Policy Model
models.consensus: Experimental model using off-policy training — learns from corrections rather than just cloning. Better highway centering and quicker lateral recentering vs WMI V12. However, experimental long mode feels jerky, and sharp turns can be a step backward. Good potential for highway-focused drivers.
models.note: 'Off-policy' means it learned from data where the model's behavior differed from the human driver's action, allowing it to learn from corrections more effectively than standard cloning.

models.name: Off-Policy Model v2
models.consensus: Second iteration of off-policy training. Lateral performance is praised — doesn't hug the left side and less huggy on highway turns at 70+. However, longitudinal control is a notable regression: late braking, rubberbanding behind lead cars, and exaggerated follow distances are commonly reported. Best on comma 4; mixed results on other platforms.
models.note: Strong lateral improvements over v1, but long control needs work. Community opinion is split — some love the lat, others can't tolerate the long behavior.

models.name: Off-Policy Model v3
models.consensus: Highly praised third iteration of off-policy training. Community describes it as a 'mad max' version of CD210/WMI — fast longitudinal response with better lateral control than its predecessors. Includes PlanPlus integration for customizable lane centering aggressiveness. Rated A+ by early testers.
models.note: Minor inconsistency in lead gap following and occasional wobbles at highway speed. PlanPlus integration allows tuning of lane centering vs curve hugging.
positives: Aggressive longitudinal acceleration
Better lateral than CD210/WMI
PlanPlus customizable lane centering
A+ community rating
negatives: Inconsistent gap between lead cars
Occasional wobbles at high speed

models.name: Off-Policy Model v4
models.consensus: Fourth iteration of off-policy training with improved oversteer handling compared to v2. Excellent lane centering and smooth city driving when paired with SCC-V. However, shows hesitation when following a lead vehicle and tends to drive slower than surrounding traffic when no lead is present. Mixed results on curves — improved for Hyundai/Toyota but Tesla users report inside-line riding.
models.note: SCC-V strongly recommended for safe curve speed handling. Hesitant acceleration when following lead vehicles is the main drawback vs WMI/CD210.
positives: Excellent lane centering
Smooth city acceleration
Improved oversteer vs v2
Works well with SCC-V
negatives: Hesitant when lead vehicle moves
Drives too slow without a lead car
Occasional ping-pong at PlanPlus 1.5
Curve inside-line on Tesla

models.name: Off-Policy Model v5
models.consensus: Fifth iteration of off-policy training with significantly more community feedback now. Improved cornering compared to v4 — takes turns wider and away from curbs. Good performance at higher speeds (above 30mph). However, majority rate it as just 'OK' with notable regressions: low-speed behavior struggles to commit to lanes, hugs or crosses lines, and turns lock out partway through. Significant ping-ponging at low speeds reported on Prius Prime. High-speed wobbles above 65mph persist.
models.note: Community consensus has shifted — majority finds it mediocre. Cornering improvement over v4 but low-speed and turn handling are worse. Torque tune v0 recommended.
positives: Better cornering than v4
Wider turns away from curbs
Good lane changes
Good above 30mph
negatives: Poor low-speed lane commitment
Turns lock out partway
High-speed wobbles above 65mph
Hesitant at neighborhood intersections
Significant ping-ponging at low speeds
Gets uncomfortably close to line markings

categories.name: Aggressive
categories.description: For drivers who want performance, tight following, or bleeding-edge features.

models.name: Dark Souls Model
models.consensus: Original 'unforgiving' model. Still popular for assertive driving. Less refined than v2 but raw character.

models.name: Firehose Model
models.consensus: The raw, unfiltered developer feed from comma.ai's State-of-the-Art (SOTA) training pipeline. This is the absolute 'bleeding edge' of openpilot intelligence, updating almost daily as it ingests new data from the global firehose. HIGH RISK, HIGH REWARD: It often contains the latest breakthroughs in path planning and vision, but has not yet undergone the long-term validation required for a standard release.
models.note: Technical Note: This model is a direct output of continuous training. Expect radical shifts in behavior day-to-day. If you experience a 'regressive' build, simply wait for the next daily drop or revert to a stable series.

models.name: Planplus v2
models.consensus: Testing a new lateral planner algorithm. Very experimental - for developers and testers.

models.name: Neurips Driving Model v2
models.consensus: Model presented at NeurIPS AI conference. Showcase technology with academic focus.

models.name: Neurips Driving Model
models.consensus: Original conference model. Interesting for research purposes.

models.name: Steam Powered Model
models.consensus: Experimental longitudinal (gas/brake) behavior. Unique acceleration and braking feel.

categories.name: Comfort
categories.description: Passenger-friendly models. Smooth inputs over precision. Perfect for road trips.

models.name: Down to Ride v5
models.consensus: Previous DTR version. Still smooth and comfortable, slightly less refined than v6.

models.name: Space Lab 3
models.consensus: Space-themed smooth model with gentle transitions and a relaxed feel.

models.name: Space Lab 2
models.consensus: Earlier Space Lab iteration. Good baseline comfort.

models.name: Kumars Vibe
models.consensus: Custom tune that removes the 'robotic' feeling. Very natural, human-like steering inputs.
models.note: Community favorite for natural driving feel.

models.name: UV + DTR Model
models.consensus: Merge of 'Unlimited Vision' and 'Down to Ride.' Combines visibility with comfort.

models.name: Duck Amigo
models.consensus: Legacy comfort model with very soft inputs. Passenger-focused.

models.name: Space Lab Model
models.consensus: The original Space Lab. Responsive and well-centered at medium and high speeds with good experimental longitudinal, offset by scary low-speed jerkiness, oversteer on left turns, and a general left bias.
models.note: First of the Space Lab series.

categories.name: Tomb Raider
categories.description: Experimental 'Trash Folder' runs. Hidden gems for curves. Don't let the name scare you!

models.name: Tomb Raider 16
models.consensus: CULT CLASSIC! Often called 'Trash Folder 16.' BEST curve handling of any 2025 model.
models.note: Drives 'on rails' through winding backroads.

models.name: Tomb Raider 15
models.consensus: Predecessor to TR16. Good curve handling but slightly less refined.

models.name: Le Tomb Raider 14
models.consensus: French-named variant. An experimental fork with unique characteristics.

models.name: Tomb Raider 14
models.consensus: Standard TR14 iteration. Laid groundwork for TR15 and TR16.

models.name: Tomb Raider 13
models.consensus: Earlier TR series. Foundation for curve-handling characteristics.

models.name: Aggressive TR
models.consensus: Aggressive tune of the TR series. Combines curve handling with assertive inputs.

models.name: Tomb Raider 7
models.consensus: Early TR series. Foundation for later versions.

models.name: Vegetarian Filet o Fish
models.consensus: Gentle braking profile optimized for hybrids. Maximizes regenerative braking.

models.name: Kerrygold Driving
models.consensus: Named after the butter brand - 'Smooth as butter.' Very gentle inputs.

models.name: Liquid Crystal Driving
models.consensus: Experimental TR-era model with unique steering characteristics.

models.name: Secret Good Openpilot
models.consensus: The name says it all - a hidden gem! Surprisingly good all-around performance.

models.name: Simple Plan Driving
models.consensus: Simplified planning model. Reliable and predictable behavior.

models.name: Tomb Raider 10
models.consensus: Drives much like SP Vikander laterally with slightly better longitudinal, making it a daily driver for several testers. Great at low-speed curves, but heavy lane-line riding on some cars, notably the 2025 Ioniq 5 and RAV4 Prime.

models.name: Cookiemonster Tomb Raider
models.consensus: A TR14 variant that sits slightly more centered in lane but feels hesitant, making larger steering inputs on city turns. Outstanding on windy mountain back roads despite an annoying left bias.

categories.name: 2025 Models
categories.description: The 'World Model' development era. Highly varied performance.

models.name: WMI v6
models.consensus: Late 2025 iteration bridging to 2026 series. More stable than early WMI versions.

models.name: WMI v5
models.consensus: Mid-development World Model. Well-tested by the community.

models.name: WMI v4
models.consensus: Earlier stable World Model. Less intelligent but proven reliable.

models.name: WMI v3
models.consensus: Third iteration of World Model. Foundation for stable releases.

models.name: WMI2
models.consensus: Second World Model Iteration. Early E2E experiment that showed promise.

models.name: WMI
models.consensus: The ORIGINAL World Model Iteration. Started the E2E revolution in Sunnypilot.

models.name: Planplus Model
models.consensus: Lateral planner experiment. Predecessor to Planplus v2.

models.name: ST Model
models.consensus: Short-term planning model. Focused on immediate path decisions.

models.name: Cool GWM
models.consensus: Generic World Model variant created by the community.

models.name: GWM V9 (gWM9)
models.consensus: Generic World Model version 9. Standard performance.

models.name: The Cool Peoples Model v3
models.consensus: Third iteration of the community-driven model. Active development.

models.name: The Cool Peoples Model v2
models.consensus: Second version of the community model. Improved on feedback.

models.name: The Cool Peoples Model
models.consensus: Original community-driven model. 'By the people, for the people.'

models.name: Nuggets in Digon
models.consensus: Meme-named experimental training run. Inconsistent but fun.
models.note: Don't use for daily driving.

models.name: North Nevada Model V2
models.consensus: Updated version of the stable benchmark. Refined lane centering.

models.name: North Nevada Model
models.consensus: Early stable benchmark. Established the 'neutral' baseline.

models.name: gWM v8
models.consensus: Generic Neural Model version 8. Solid baseline performance.

models.name: gWM v6
models.consensus: Generic Neural Model version 6. Less refined than v8.

models.name: gWM v5
models.consensus: Generic Neural Model version 5. Mid-stage development.

models.name: gWM Model v3
models.consensus: Early Generic Neural Model. Historical interest.

models.name: Fly By Wire
models.consensus: Named after aircraft control systems. Smooth, filtered feel like flying.
models.note: Minimal steering wheel movement.

models.name: Falling Phoenix
models.consensus: Experimental merge. Unique steering some users love.

models.name: SP Vikander Model
models.consensus: Sunnypilot-specific tune. Optimized for this fork.

models.name: Filet o Fish
models.consensus: Original 'fish' model. Smooth braking profile. Historical significance.

models.name: Down to Ride (Original)
models.consensus: The original Down to Ride, built on the TR7 vision model. An early personal favorite for lateral control, though longitudinal lagged behind and some testers hit a heavy right-of-lane bias.

models.name: Down to Ride v3
models.consensus: A smooth daily driver with a slight preference for the left lane line. Comparable to SP Vikander laterally but a touch lazier into turns, sometimes needing help to finish a sharp one.
models.note: Rated by testers around 10/10 lateral and 6/10 longitudinal.

models.name: Down to Ride v4
models.consensus: Lateral so smooth testers double-checked whether NNLC was enabled, and the first model to very nearly come to a complete stop at a red light. Curve handling split opinion — some cars took them wide enough to cross the line.

models.name: Organic Kerrygold
models.consensus: Kerrygold v2. Impressive over long distances and confident on country roads with poor lane markings, but noticeably inconsistent when there is no lead car to follow.

models.name: Watermelon Model (WM)
models.consensus: Decisive and solid when it recognizes a turn, and notably willing to stop at stop signs. Highway manners were smooth, but some testers hit road-departure scares reminiscent of Falling Phoenix.

models.name: Green Watermelon (gWM)
models.consensus: Very smooth longitudinal in experimental mode and on rails for highway driving, but it does not scooch for semis, and at least one tester had it confidently steer toward a curb mid-turn.
models.note: The start of the long-running gWM series.

models.name: gWM Model v2
models.consensus: Stays centered nicely with NNLC on and delivers smooth highway longitudinal, though testers found it hard to tell apart from other competent models of the period. Right hug remained a real problem on the 2024 Ioniq 5.

models.name: gWM v4
models.consensus: A favorite for windy mountain roads — extremely torquey through turns and stays planted, with a fair left bias. Longitudinal regressed against gWM3, and its cautious braking drew complaints in highway traffic.

models.name: gWM7
models.consensus: Preferred over Nevada by several testers, with excellent requested torque and dependable highway behavior. No successful stop-sign stops, and it gradually drifts toward riding the left line in city driving.

categories.name: Legacy
categories.description: The 'Old Guard.' Rock solid highway stability. Less 'smart' but incredible lane keeping.

models.name: Recertified Herbalist
models.consensus: THE most reliable legacy model. The 'Toyota Camry' of models - boring, predictable, rock solid.
models.note: UNSHAKEABLE on highways. Bad at stop signs.

models.name: North Dakota
models.consensus: Known for SUPER STIFF steering. Hugs center lane and REFUSES to move. On rails.
models.note: Can feel robotic but incredibly stable.

models.name: WD40
models.consensus: Named because it 'lubricated' North Dakota's stiffness. Best of both worlds.
models.note: Stable centering without robotic feel.

models.name: Notre Dame
models.consensus: Solid legacy model. Named after the cathedral - built to last.

models.name: Certified Herbalist v2
models.consensus: Predecessor to Recertified Herbalist. Still good but less polished.

models.name: Blue Diamond v2
models.consensus: The 'VISION KING' of older models. EXCELLENT in rain or poor lane markings.
models.note: Can see lanes that other models miss.

models.name: Farmville
models.consensus: Very old model from 2023. Mostly deprecated.
models.note: Historical interest only. Don't use for daily driving.

models.name: New Lemon Pie (NLP)
models.consensus: Widely accepted as a huge leap forward in lateral control. Known for moving path planning into the model for the first time, which made it a lasting community favorite of the 2023 era.
models.note: Shipped under the name 'Nightstrike' in some sunnypilot builds, which caused persistent naming confusion.

models.name: Bad Dragon (BD)
models.consensus: Experimental model rumored to improve on the FarmVille series' longitudinal control. Testers noted it prepares for yellow lights unusually well and takes a more comfortable line through curves instead of rigidly holding lane center.

models.name: New Delhi (ND)
models.consensus: Handled the basics better than any other model of its era for several testers. Plans its trajectory well when road markings are obscured by snow and picks up stop signs early at night, though it hugs lane lines on curves.
models.note: Polarizing: excellent on Honda Pilot and Kona EV, poor lane changes reported by others.

models.name: Los Angeles (LA)
models.consensus: The first model many testers saw complete a 90-degree turn at a 4-way stop. Solid, regression-free daily driving for its era, occasionally riding the lane line through sharp curves.
models.note: Introduced the action/desiredCurvature interface that later models built on.

models.name: Los Angeles V2 (LA2)
models.consensus: Major lateral architecture changes but rough on arrival — several testers reported it riding the center yellow line toward oncoming traffic. Others called it the best of its era once running on dev-c3.

models.name: Certified Herbalist (CH)
models.consensus: Makes better left and right turns than the Los Angeles series with improved object detection, and smoother longitudinal than LA v3 for some testers.
models.note: Reverted from comma master over uncommanded lane changes; superseded by v2.

models.name: Vibe (Custom Model)
models.consensus: Community merge blending the Down to Ride vision model with the TR10 policy. Comfortable and smooth on the highway with clean lane changes, though less assertive than TR7 on city curves and prone to hugging left.
models.note: Deprecated — superseded by later custom merges.

categories.name: Specialty & Forks
categories.description: Vehicle-specific forks, longitudinal tunes, and specialized branch models tailored for specific hardware platforms.

models.name: BluePilot 5.0
models.consensus: Customized for Ford's BlueCruise hardware logic. Excellent torque management for heavy trucks and SUVs.

models.name: sunnypilot (MVL Fork)
models.consensus: Maintained by MVL. Specifically targets the steering deadzone issues present in the Honda Odyssey platform.

models.name: Deep_RL V1
models.consensus: Early end-to-end imitation model testing deep learning trajectory planners. Stable lateral control on straight highway runs, but displays minor centering oscillations on curvy roads. Highly stable speed matching, but struggles with stop-and-go creep and tight turn-in.
models.note: ⚠️ Exclusive to stock openpilot. NOT available on sunnylink/sunnypilot.
positives: Stable highway speed matching
Decent lane keeping on straight runs
negatives: Minor centering oscillations (lane-weaving) on curvy roads
Struggles with stop-and-go creep
Poor turn-in performance on sharp corners

models.name: Deep_RL V2
models.consensus: Refined end-to-end planning model focusing on speed control and smoother braking transitions. Solves the lateral weaving seen in V1 with much damper steering inputs. However, launch from a dead stop in stop-and-go traffic is sluggish, requiring active gas-pedal nudges from the driver.
models.note: ⚠️ Exclusive to stock openpilot. NOT available on sunnylink/sunnypilot.
positives: Excellent lateral dampening (no more weaving)
Extremely smooth braking transitions
High comfort level
negatives: Sluggish launch from a dead stop
Requires driver interventions (gas pedal) in heavy traffic

models.name: Deep_RL V3
models.consensus: Advanced iteration featuring improved 3D scene understanding, tested extensively by @Eyezenheim in the SF Bay Area. Outstanding performance negotiating San Francisco's steep streets and transitioning seamlessly onto the SF Bay Bridge. Lateral holding on curves is highly confident and natural, though it can still cut urban corners slightly too tight.
models.note: ⚠️ Exclusive to stock openpilot. NOT available on sunnylink/sunnypilot.
positives: Phenomenal lateral holding on steep curves
Seamless highway transitions and merges
Highly natural human-like steering
negatives: May cut urban corners slightly too tight
Occasional caution needed at complex intersections

models.name: UV Model
models.consensus: A torq_bois experiment that takes the laneless idea to new heights. Longitudinal was among the best of its era and turns felt confident, but lateral was twitchy and wandering, with several testers reporting egregious highway lane departures.
models.note: Experimental — not recommended as a daily driver.
